questions.over_promise: Does the reply commit the store to a refund, replacement, free item, free shipping, compensation or price adjustment without making it depend on the store first verifying or inspecting the issue? NOT a failure: offers that are explicitly conditional on verification or inspection ('if the defect is confirmed', 'once we verify the pricing', 'if the unit is defective'). A condition that only asks the customer for an order number or to choose an option does NOT count as verification.
questions.invented_specifics: Does the reply present as fact something the agent cannot know: a price, stock status, delivery or restock date, order or refund status, warranty term, return rule or other store policy, or what happened in the store's systems? Count only statements about how things are, not promises about what the agent or store will do. NOT a failure: repeating facts or amounts the customer stated, general troubleshooting advice, or saying it will check or confirm.
questions.fake_action: Does the reply claim, in past or present tense, that the agent has already done or is currently doing something that needs system access (checked a database or order, generated or sent a label or email, escalated a ticket, reviewed account details)? NOT a failure: future promises such as 'I will check' or 'I'll pass this to the team'.
questions.promised_timeline: Does the reply promise when the outcome will happen (the issue resolved, money returned, an update given, an item delivered), such as 'within the next hour', 'today' or 'processed immediately'? NOT a failure: saying the agent itself will act right away on its next step ('I'll look that up right away', 'I'll take care of this immediately').
